acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc:
A new documentary called The Boys and the Bees captures a moment where a six-year-old has a very unlikely wish, and his dad decides to grant it. Host Ira Glass talks with filmmaker Arielle Knight about what happens next.
Arielle Knight is an award-winning director and producer of The Boys and the Bees. The film is currently touring festivals worldwide and will air on POV on PBS in the fall of 2026.
acts.credits: By Ira Glass; Produced by Valerie Kipnis

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
John Tothill tells the story of Edward Dando, a 19th-century British glutton who would eat hundreds of oysters at a time and then run out on the check. John makes the case that we should all be more like Edward Dando.
John’s show was directed by Alex Cartlidge and Kathryn Craigmyle. He’s on tour across the UK right now, details at @johntothill.
acts.credits: By John Tothill; Produced by Aviva DeKornfeld
acts.title: Lessons in Shellfishness

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Producer Tobin Low listens in as Evan Roberts calls up an ex for the first time in years and tries to make the case that they should have been friends all along.
Evan wrote about his conversations with all his exes on his Substack, Don't Be Precious, Darling.
acts.title: The Joy of Ex

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Producer Zoe Chace brings us a dispatch from a courtroom in Texas this week, where on the very first day of a landmark federal trial about Antifa, the judge makes an unusual decision that no one sees coming.
acts.credits: By Zoe Chace and Ira Glass
acts.title: The Lawyer, The Judge and The Wardrobe
